features.title: Features
features.subtitle: What ships today, what is coming next, and what is still being built
features.item.timetable.title: Timetable
features.item.timetable.summary: Multi-source import, multiple schedules, week and month views, class reminders.
features.item.timetable.description: Import from the undergraduate and graduate systems, WakeUp files and share codes, third-party timetables, or edit by hand. Group multiple schedules, switch between week and month views, and get class reminders that stay in sync with your widgets.
features.item.agenda.title: Agenda & to-dos
features.item.agenda.summary: Courses, schedules, tasks, notes and medication in one place, with recurrence and reminders.
features.item.agenda.description: Items come in five kinds — courses, schedules, tasks, notes and medication — with flexible recurrence (multiple times a day, per-weekday times, month-day rules, interval cycles), swipe actions, class and task reminders, and agenda data synced to widgets.
features.item.freeClassrooms.title: Free classrooms
features.item.freeClassrooms.summary: Search free rooms on several axes, with your own clashes filtered out.
features.item.freeClassrooms.description: Search by date, campus, building and period. Rooms that clash with your own timetable are excluded automatically, and any result can be turned into an agenda item in one tap.
features.item.librarySeats.title: Library study seats
features.item.librarySeats.summary: Native seat search, booking and cancellation.
features.item.librarySeats.description: Query library spaces, dates, time slots and individual seats through the native API. Create or cancel bookings, keep a list of your own, and get agenda reminders.
features.item.sportsVenues.title: Sports venue booking
features.item.sportsVenues.summary: Book venues, activities and slots, and manage the orders.
features.item.sportsVenues.description: Browse venues and available slots, then book, pay, cancel and review your orders. Bookings can be written straight into your agenda.
features.item.universityTimetable.title: University-wide timetable
features.item.universityTimetable.summar: Browse every course on offer and filter out the clashes.
features.item.universityTimetable.descri: Browse the whole university timetable by academic year and term, search for courses, and narrow the results against your own schedule to find the ones you can actually attend or add.
features.item.academicProgress.title: Academic progress
features.item.academicProgress.summary: Degree plan, progress and credit totals.
features.item.academicProgress.descripti: Shows your major, your degree plan, the credits you have earned and the courses still outstanding, so you can track how much of the programme is left.
features.item.grades.title: Grades
features.item.grades.summary: Multi-channel import, GPA algorithms and grade trends.
features.item.grades.description: Import from the undergraduate system, trusted electronic credentials and the professional development system. Switch GPA algorithms, follow grade trends, export a transcript PDF, filter by term, and lock the screen behind biometrics.
features.item.universityCalendar.title: University calendar
features.item.universityCalendar.summary: WHU's calendar and term dates, whenever you need them.
features.item.universityCalendar.descrip: Every year of WHU's calendar in one place: term start and end dates, holidays and the teaching schedule at a glance.
features.item.courseReviews.title: Grade distributions & reviews
features.item.courseReviews.summary: Grade distributions, course reviews and anonymous submission.
features.item.courseReviews.description: See how a course's grades are distributed and read its reviews, or submit your own anonymously. Small samples are aggregated to protect privacy, continuing the data lineage of WHU.sb.
features.item.xuexitong.title: Chaoxing account
features.item.xuexitong.summary: Bind your Xuexitong account; credentials stay in on-device secure storage.
features.item.xuexitong.description: Bind Xuexitong (Chaoxing) by password or SMS code. Credentials are kept in this device's secure storage and isolated per WHU account, laying the groundwork for course and check-in features later on.
features.item.xiji.title: Xiji course platform
features.item.xiji.summary: A second course platform with assignment and exam reminders.
features.item.xiji.description: Sign in to the Xiji (PTA) course platform via CAS or a platform account, list enrolled courses, view descriptions, assignments and exams with due times, set reminder lead times, and project assignment deadlines into your agenda and timetable.
features.item.courseSpace.title: Course space
features.item.courseSpace.summary: A shared course directory with teachers and resources.
features.item.courseSpace.description: Aggregates teaching classes into a unified course directory by term, with standardised course names and numbers. Open a course to see its classes and shared information, teacher profiles, resources and audit/trust status; administrators can maintain the full catalogue and classes.
features.item.majorInfo.title: Majors & programmes
features.item.majorInfo.summary: Browse majors, training plans and employment outcomes.
features.item.majorInfo.description: Browse the school's faculty → college → major hierarchy, with training goals, positioning, features and teaching plans, plus employment-outcome charts (type, province, employer and industry). Colleges offer an in-app preview of the training-plan PDF.
features.item.csEban.title: CS Yiban
features.item.csEban.summary: Awards, disciplinary records and evaluation points for the School of Computer Science.
features.item.csEban.description: Connects to the School of Computer Science's Yiban (易办) affairs platform to view undergraduate awards and disciplinary records (category, level, reason, points, issuer) and ideological-evaluation points (total, grade, details), with date-range filtering; credentials stay on-device.
features.item.libraryLoans.title: Library borrowing
features.item.libraryLoans.summary: Catalog search, loans, renewals, reservations and due-date reminders.
features.item.libraryLoans.description: A native WHU OPAC client: search the catalogue (field, year, language and material filters), view holdings and call numbers, place holds with a pickup location and validity, list current reservations and loans with one-tap renewal, review borrowing-history statistics and get local due-date and overdue reminders.
features.item.ecard.title: Luojia E-card & payment code
features.item.ecard.summary: A native payment code that refreshes itself — and works from your watch.
features.item.ecard.description: Entry point for the Luojia E-card, with balance and transaction history. The native payment code refreshes every minute, with the web version as a fallback, and is available from Apple Watch and from home-screen shortcuts.
features.item.shuttleBus.title: Shuttle bus
features.item.shuttleBus.summary: Live positions, route lookup and arrival alerts.
features.item.shuttleBus.description: Look up routes and live vehicle positions, overlay them on the campus map, and get arrival alerts in the background. Syncs with iOS Live Activities and watch snapshots.
features.item.campusMap.title: Campus map
features.item.campusMap.summary: Native maps, place search and facility layers.
features.item.campusMap.description: A native map implementation, not an embedded web page. Combined place search, layers for car parks, entrances, AEDs and campus facilities, and a choice of vector or satellite imagery.
features.item.hospital.title: Hospital services
features.item.hospital.summary: Patient card, appointments, queue status, invoices and reports.
features.item.hospital.description: Manage your patient card; view and cancel appointments, follow the outpatient queue, check opening hours, see paid and unpaid invoices, and read lab and examination reports.
features.item.utilities.title: Utility bills & water codes
features.item.utilities.summary: Dormitory water and electricity, payments, and hot-water codes.
features.item.utilities.description: Check your dormitory's water and electricity usage, pay online, and get a low-balance alert. Hot-water codes are ready the moment you need one.
features.item.notifications.title: Campus notifications
features.item.notifications.summary: Notifications and to-dos aggregated from the WHU message centre.
features.item.notifications.description: Aggregates the WHU message centre with all / notifications / to-dos views, full message detail and unread badges.
features.item.smartLuojia.title: Smart Luojia
features.item.smartLuojia.summary: Straight to the official portal, already carrying your campus identity.
features.item.smartLuojia.description: The Smart Luojia portal, embedded and reusing your campus session, so the everyday university services stop asking you to log in again.
features.item.campusNetwork.title: Campus network
features.item.campusNetwork.summary: Plans, devices, top-up, pause and resume.
features.item.campusNetwork.description: Check your plan, pause and resume it (unused days roll over), authenticate through the portal automatically, switch carrier, manage connected devices and top up. On iOS it can join at system level.
features.item.campusVpn.title: Campus VPN
features.item.campusVpn.summary: Sangfor aTrust split tunnelling with connectivity tests.
features.item.campusVpn.description: Connect to WHU's aTrust VPN with an in-app proxy or a system-level TUN, split-tunnelling rules, two-factor challenges and a built-in web connectivity test.
features.item.forum.title: Forum: Luojia Shelter
features.item.forum.summary: Posts, comments, attachments, reputation and moderation.
features.item.forum.description: A community forum with posts, comments, boards, attachments, search, reputation, leaderboards and a public moderation log. The tab is hidden by default and can be turned on under Settings → Navigation.
features.item.social.title: Community social
features.item.social.description: Public user profiles, a follow/block graph and in-app direct messages, sharing one account with the forum.
features.item.campusNews.title: Campus news
features.item.campusNews.summary: Subscribe to campus sources, with offline reading and full-text search.
features.item.campusNews.description: Aggregates 200+ sites and nearly a thousand columns of campus news. Subscribe by site or column, track read state, search across everything and cache for offline reading, with a built-in reading mode and text extraction that degrades gracefully when the VPN is unavailable.
features.item.dining.title: Dining
features.item.dining.summary: Campus food discovery with menus, ratings and a random picker.
features.item.dining.description: Browse dining spots and canteen floors on a map, with search, campus scoping, menus with per-item prices, ratings and reviews, opening hours and photos. A random picker (shop or dish) supports rating and price filters, and you can contribute shops, menus, hours and corrections.
features.item.ebike.title: Shared e-bikes
features.item.ebike.summary: Link e-bike accounts and unlock by scanning.
features.item.ebike.description: Link Zhiyin, Mango and other shared e-bike accounts, unlock by scanning (BLE), and view live riding status, wallet balance, ride cards, order history, unpaid-order alerts and a riding map.
features.item.lepao.title: Lepao running
features.item.lepao.summary: Your campus running records and GPS tracks.
features.item.lepao.description: Bind a Lepao campus-running account and review your per-year run history — distance, duration, pace and validity — with per-run GPS track maps and per-kilometre splits.
features.item.washing.title: Laundry
features.item.washing.summary: Check washer status and order a wash.
features.item.washing.description: Browse laundry locations by area, building and floor, view live machine status (idle, running or fault) and remaining time, choose a wash mode (price and minutes) and place an order, then hand off payment to the operator's mini-program.
features.item.voteTicket.title: Ticket grabbing
features.item.voteTicket.summary: Grab event tickets and help others out.
features.item.voteTicket.description: Browse WHU event ticket-grabs, view posters, rules and quotas, participate to mint a personal assistance QR, scan or paste someone's code to assist them, and use a mutual-aid hall showing received, given and net standing with one-tap batch assist.
features.item.medication.title: Medication
features.item.medication.summary: Dose schedule, stock and adherence tracking over your agenda.
features.item.medication.description: Manage each drug's dose, next intake and remaining stock on top of your agenda, log extra doses, refill stock, review a 30-day adherence summary, and import medTimer backups or export CSV history.
features.item.mentalHealth.title: Mental health
features.item.mentalHealth.summary: A psychological scale library with scored results.
features.item.mentalHealth.description: A remotely synced library of psychological scales (search and category filter). Take a scale with batch viewing, auto-saved drafts and sex-specific norms; results show total and factor scores, level, a radar breakdown and crisis flags, with a local history.
features.item.menstrualCycle.title: Period tracker
features.item.menstrualCycle.description: Log flow, symptoms, mood and notes per day, with a calendar shading recorded, predicted and fertile days, next-period/ovulation/fertile-window prediction with confidence, cycle statistics and adjustable cycle and period length — entirely on-device.
features.item.aiAssistant.title: AI assistant
features.item.aiAssistant.summary: A multi-model agent that can operate campus services.
features.item.aiAssistant.description: Built-in and custom models, multimodal attachments, on-device and cloud voice input, read-aloud, image generation, web search, MCP, skills and assistants. A confirmation bridge offers semi-automatic and fully automatic modes; the tools can read and manage your timetable, grades, mailbox and campus service data, and can start utility or network payments once you confirm.
features.item.weather.title: Weather
features.item.weather.summary: Multi-source forecasts, AQI, precipitation and alerts.
features.item.weather.description: Mi Weather, Open-Meteo and AccuWeather are each queried directly for what they do best: hourly forecasts, air quality, pollen counts and official weekly reports, precipitation, alerts, caching and retries. Every source substitution or fallback is traceable, and a strict mode is available.
features.item.coremail.title: Coremail mailbox
features.item.coremail.summary: Campus mail, message detail and unread badges.
features.item.coremail.description: A native Coremail client with SSO sign-in, client-specific passwords, an inbox, composing and sending, safely rendered message detail and unread badges. The mailbox is also open to the AI agent for searching, organising and drafting.
features.item.wallpapers.title: Wallpaper centre
features.item.wallpapers.summary: Local files, image URLs, Bing daily, and per-page configuration.
features.item.wallpapers.description: Choose no wallpaper, a local image, an online image URL, or Bing's daily pick at random. The timetable, campus, settings, task list, forum and AI pages can each be configured separately, with an adjustable dark overlay.
features.item.hotUpdate.title: Signed hot updates
features.item.hotUpdate.summary: Signed parser scripts, so API changes need no new release.
features.item.hotUpdate.description: This site distributes Ed25519-signed QuickJS parser scripts. When a campus API changes the parser can be hot-updated, instead of everyone waiting for an app release.
features.item.appUpdate.title: In-app updates
features.item.appUpdate.summary: Check for a new version and be walked through installing it.
features.item.appUpdate.description: Checks GitHub Releases for updates. On Android it suggests the right ABI upgrade and guides the install; on desktop it opens the release page in your browser.
features.item.appleShortcuts.title: Apple Shortcuts
features.item.appleShortcuts.summary: Shortcuts can call the app's audited tools.
features.item.appleShortcuts.description: macOS Shortcuts can call audited app tools such as the university calendar, timetable, grades and free classrooms. Anything that writes needs confirmation.
features.item.widgets.title: Home-screen widgets
features.item.widgets.summary: Four widgets across Android, iOS, macOS and Linux.
features.item.widgets.description: Agenda list, today's classes, countdown, and this week's classes — four widgets covering Android, iOS, the macOS menu bar and the Linux tray, plus iOS Live Activities.
features.item.watch.title: Watch companion
features.item.watch.summary: Syncs with Apple Watch and Huawei, HarmonyOS, vivo and Xiaomi watches.
features.item.watch.description: Apple Watch can present the E-card payment code and sync agenda items and the shuttle bus; Huawei, HarmonyOS, vivo and Xiaomi watches sync agenda and shuttle-bus snapshots.
features.item.appShortcuts.title: App shortcuts
features.item.appShortcuts.summary: Long-press the icon to jump straight to what you use most.
features.item.appShortcuts.description: Android App Shortcuts and iOS Quick Actions go directly to the E-card payment code, study-seat booking, the AI assistant and more, and appear according to your sign-in state.
features.item.accountSecurity.title: Accounts & security
features.item.accountSecurity.summary: CAS, Luotopia accounts, passkeys and device trust.
features.item.accountSecurity.descriptio: WHU CAS and Luotopia accounts are kept separate. Passkeys, multiple sessions, device trust, API credentials and a biometric lock on grades are all supported, and diagnostic telemetry can be turned off.
features.item.languages.title: Multiple languages
features.item.languages.summary: Eleven languages across twelve script variants, with localised time formats.
features.item.languages.description: Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Cantonese (simplified and traditional), English, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Vietnamese — eleven languages across twelve script variants.
features.item.multiAccount.title: Multi-account switching
features.item.multiAccount.summary: Credentials isolated per WHU account, and switchable.
features.item.multiAccount.description: A device can remember several WHU accounts and switch between them quickly. VPN, mailbox and Xuexitong credentials are isolated per account and never cross over.
features.item.thirdPartyAccounts.title: Third-party account linking
features.item.thirdPartyAccounts.summary: Authorised linking for third-party accounts such as Ham.
features.item.thirdPartyAccounts.descrip: Manage external accounts in one place under Other accounts. Authorised linking and unlinking for Ham is available, with more third parties to come.
features.item.studyMaterials.title: Shared study materials
features.item.studyMaterials.summary: Search materials by course, teacher and term.
features.item.studyMaterials.description: Planned: server-side search, upload, download, favourites and review status, with materials organised by course, teacher and term.
features.item.gradeEnhancements.title: Grades, enhanced
features.item.gradeEnhancements.summary: Term comparison, summary export and course-identifier links.
features.item.gradeEnhancements.descript: Building on the existing grade trends: term-over-term comparison, summary export and linking through to course identifiers.
features.item.recurrenceEnhancements.sum: Expanding recurring items and acting on the whole series.
features.item.recurrenceEnhancements.des: Expanding a recurring item into its instances, completing and restoring them, and operating on the series as a whole.
features.item.widgetEnhancements.title: Widgets, enhanced
features.item.widgetEnhancements.summary: Improving Android and exploring more platform entry points.
features.item.widgetEnhancements.descrip: Continuing to improve the Android widgets and looking at entry points on more desktop platforms.
features.item.standaloneWeb.title: Standalone web edition
features.item.standaloneWeb.summary: Flutter Web is retired; a standalone web product is planned.
features.item.standaloneWeb.description: The Flutter Web compatibility layer and its release artefacts are no longer maintained. A standalone web product will start once the requirements and the server-side proxy capabilities are settled.
brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Luotopia brand assets: the 3D marks, vector and bitmap logo downloads, brand colours and usage rules.
brand.subtitle: Luotopia's marks, colours and usage rules, for the media, for developers and for campus partners.
brand.logo3d.heading: 3D marks
brand.logo3d.blurb: Both logos in three dimensions. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.
brand.logo3d.wu.title: Wu · stacked slices
brand.logo3d.wu.subtitle: The Wu character is cut into fourteen stone slabs that offset layer by layer and settle into place in turn. It echoes the stacked rock of Luojia Hill; turn the viewpoint and the layering and the depth become visible.
brand.logo3d.luo.title: Luo · growth
brand.logo3d.luo.subtitle: The Luo character is written as calligraphy: translucent jade-like strokes grow in one by one, following the stroke order, with a faint new-sprout glimmer at the brush tip, and sway lightly in the wind once the character is complete.
brand.logo3d.hint: 3D · drag or flick to rotate · scroll to zoom
brand.flat.heading: Flat marks
brand.flat.blurb: Vector (SVG) scales without loss for the web and for print; bitmap (PNG, 1024×1024 with transparency) suits app icons and other raster contexts. Both are available in full colour and as a monochrome white version.
brand.mark.wu.name: Wu
brand.mark.wu.meaning: A geometric transformation of the Wu character from Wuhan University's name, its horizontal strokes stacked to echo the Luojia hills. It is also the app's default icon.
brand.mark.luo.name: Luo
brand.mark.luo.meaning: The Luo character is taken from Luojia. A geometric jade radical on the left, a single cursive stroke on the right; used as the alternate icon and as the basis for brand extensions.
brand.colors.heading: Brand colours
brand.colors.blurb: Click a swatch to copy its HEX.
brand.color.wu.name: Wu · Mountain Blue
brand.color.luo.name: Luo · Ink Green
brand.usage.heading: Usage rules
brand.usage.blurb: These conventions keep the marks consistent across every context.
brand.usage.sizing.title: Size and clear space
brand.usage.sizing.minSize: Minimum height {digital} on screen; minimum height {print} in print.
brand.usage.sizing.clearSpace: Keep clear space of at least {ratio} of the mark's height on all four sides, so it never crowds the elements around it.
brand.usage.sizing.vector: Prefer the vector SVG; export the bitmap PNG at 2× / 3× as needed for high-density screens.
brand.usage.sizing.contrast: Use the monochrome white version on dark backgrounds and the full-colour version on light ones, so contrast stays sufficient.
brand.usage.licence.title: Licence and attribution
brand.usage.licence.owner: The marks are copyright {owner}, and identify the Luotopia app and its official content.
brand.usage.licence.nonCommercial: Press reviews and non-commercial use by campus partners are welcome, provided the mark stays whole — no recolouring and no distortion.
brand.usage.licence.commercial: For commercial partnerships, derivative work or large-scale distribution, please get in touch through the {community} first to obtain a licence.
brand.usage.licence.threeD: The 3D versions on this page are for demonstration only; use the flat marks above for anything formal.
brand.usage.donts.title: Please do not
brand.usage.donts: Stretch it, squash it or change its aspect ratio
Recolour it (other than to the monochrome white version)
Add outlines, shadows, gradients or any other extra effect
Place it directly on a cluttered or low-contrast background
Substitute a low-resolution bitmap for the vector source file

download.install.title: Installation notes
download.install.android.body: Builds are split by ABI. On an Android phone — or on Zhuoyitong, the Android compatibility layer on HarmonyOS — take the build marked "Recommended": {arm64}. If an older device cannot install that one, try {armv7}; on an Android emulator, use {x86}. Install the APK as soon as it has downloaded. If the system warns you about an unknown source or a possible risk, allow the installation in system settings and choose to ignore the warning and continue.
download.install.apple.ios.body: {lead} all distributed through TestFlight. Open the {joinLink} to request access on an iPhone, an iPad or an Apple-silicon Mac (macOS 13.5+). A TestFlight build stays valid for 90 days and a new one ships roughly every week or two, so keeping the app updated is all it takes — turning on automatic updates is worth doing.
download.install.apple.macos.body: On macOS you can also download the {dmg} straight from a release (Apple silicon, unsigned build): drag Luotopia.app into Applications, then on first launch {openWith}, or run {xattr} in a terminal. Only ever do this for a DMG that came from this site or from an official GitHub release.
download.install.linux.body: Published per {arch} (x64 / arm64) and per {format}. Installation examples:
download.install.linux.note: Needs a reasonably recent glibc and GTK3.
download.install.harmony.body: Sideloading on HarmonyOS NEXT is difficult and nothing here is actively maintained, so the {hap} does not ship with every release. When a release does include {signedHap}, sideload it by following the {sideload} file from the same version.
download.install.harmony.note: Platform limits mean some features are hidden or reduced on HarmonyOS.

legal.terms.title: Terms of Service
legal.terms.description: Please read this agreement before you use Luotopia, so that you understand the scope of the service, the rules of use, and the boundaries around accounts and liability.
legal.terms.s1.heading: 1. Parties and Scope
legal.terms.s1.body: This agreement is entered into between ClosedWHU Team (hereinafter “we”, “us” or “our”) and the users of the Luotopia client and related services (hereinafter “you” or “your”). Luotopia is an all-in-one campus-life client for students and staff at Wuhan University, and is available on platforms including Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux.

By installing, opening or continuing to use this app, you confirm that you have read, understood and agree to this agreement, together with the Privacy Policy and the Cross-Border Data Transfer Notice that take effect alongside it. If you do not agree, please stop using the app immediately and uninstall it.

This app operates primarily as a “client”: features such as the timetable, grades, free classrooms, library seats, sports venues, the shuttle bus, campus messages and the Luojia E-card usually send requests to Wuhan University and its partners' systems through the campus unified identity authentication (CAS) session established once you authorise a sign-in; the related business data is, in principle, cached locally on your own device rather than uploaded and hosted centrally by us.
legal.terms.s2.heading: 2. Service Content and Boundaries
legal.terms.s2.body: Depending on the features of the actual version, this app may provide, including but not limited to: timetable management and multi-source import, free-classroom search, library seat booking, sports venue booking, the Luojia E-card and payment-code entry point, campus messages, shuttle-bus information, the university calendar, academic-progress and grade lookup, weather and air quality, the wallpaper centre, local agenda and notes, AI assistant conversations, home-screen widgets, and optional Luotopia account sign-in with community-related capabilities.

The availability of the campus-side features depends on the openness of Wuhan University's academic-affairs, Smart Luojia, library, venue, shuttle-bus, message and payment systems, on changes to their interfaces, and on your account permissions. We cannot guarantee that the university's systems stay available, that their fields are complete, or that what is displayed is absolutely accurate.

Some pages embed the university's or a partner's pages through a WebView (for example Smart Luojia, email, and pages related to China Construction Bank campus-card payment). These pages are operated by third parties; their interface, rules and data handling are governed by the third party's own terms, and we only provide the entry point and the necessary session hand-off.

External resources such as the developer docs, friend links and the hot-update script repository may be reached through links. Once you follow a link, the service is the responsibility of its own operator, and this does not constitute any guarantee of third-party content by this app.
legal.terms.s3.heading: 3. Accounts, Sign-In and Credentials
legal.terms.s3.body: The campus features usually require you to authenticate through Wuhan University's CAS (`cas.whu.edu.cn`). The sign-in process takes place inside the system WebView; we will not ask you to re-enter your CAS password into the app's own form for upload to our servers. After successful authentication, the app stores the session cookies / tickets needed for CAS and for business systems such as academic affairs in secure on-device storage, so that it can call the university's interfaces later.

If you use a Luotopia account (registering with or signing in to the server we operate), you need to provide information such as a username, a password and an optional email address. The server issues an access token (such as a JWT), which is kept in the secure storage of your device. The first-party server that the client connects to by default is `api-whu-sb.tsinbei.cn`; the website and static resources are at `www.whu.sb`; and `api.whu.sb` has also been used in the past. The exact endpoints follow the actual client configuration.

We may show a “Signed-in devices” list under your account. It usually includes the device name and device identifier, the sign-in IP and its location, the app version and system version, and the runtime-environment security conclusion reported by the device itself. You can revoke the session of any of these devices at any time. For details of the related processing, see the Privacy Policy.

You should keep your device, lock screen and biometric settings secure. Losses caused by a lost device, a shared device, malware, or your own disclosure of credentials are your responsibility. You can sign out of the campus account or clear the related cache in the app at any time (subject to the feature settings).

Sensitive displays such as grades can be protected with a local privacy lock (unlocked by system biometrics or the device credential). This mechanism works only on the device and does not upload your biometric data to our servers.
legal.terms.s4.heading: 4. User Conduct
legal.terms.s4.body: You must comply with the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China, with Wuhan University's rules and discipline, and with this agreement. You may not use this app for any unlawful, infringing, harassing or fraudulent activity, or for anything that endangers network security.

You may not carry out unauthorised reverse engineering, decompilation, cracking, tampering or repackaging of this app, or bypass its technical protection measures; nor may you subject the campus interfaces or this app's interfaces to high-frequency scraping, bulk automated abuse, load-based attacks, or anything that disrupts normal service.

You may not use another person's account, cookies or tokens for unauthorised access; nor may you forge a User-Agent or forge requests to impersonate the official campus client for improper purposes. For compatibility with the university's systems, this app may use a smart-campus-related client identifier in certain WebViews or requests; this is done solely for functional interoperability and does not authorise you to impersonate the official app to commit fraud.

You may not use features such as the AI assistant, messages, the forum or reviews to generate or spread content that is unlawful or non-compliant, or that infringes others' privacy or intellectual-property rights.

If we find, or have reasonable grounds to believe, that you have breached this agreement, we may restrict features, refuse service or take other reasonable measures, and we reserve the right to pursue liability in accordance with the law.
legal.terms.s5.heading: 5. AI Assistant and User-Generated Content
legal.terms.s5.body: The AI assistant feature relies on the provider, interface address, model and API key that you configure yourself. The built-in default providers may include domestic services such as SiliconFlow; you can also switch to overseas providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, xAI and Perplexity, or to a custom address.

When you use the AI, your conversation content, message history, and the local agenda summary injected to improve the experience (such as item titles, details, locations and times) are sent to the servers of the provider you choose. Do not enter sensitive information such as passwords, full identity-document numbers or payment passcodes into the conversation.
You are responsible for how you use AI output and for its consequences. AI replies may be inaccurate and do not constitute academic-affairs, legal or medical advice, or an official notice.
legal.terms.s6.heading: 6. Intellectual Property and Open Interfaces
legal.terms.s6.body: Unless otherwise stated or licensed as open source, the intellectual property in this app's name, marks, interface design, code and documentation belongs to ClosedWHU Team or the corresponding rights holders. You may not copy, distribute or use them for commercial purposes without permission.

The app client itself is not distributed as open source; however, we may provide official documentation, an open API, or community collaboration channels. When you use these open capabilities, you must follow the corresponding interface specifications and rate limits, and must not harm the stability of the service or the rights of others.

The rights in user content that you import or create through this app — such as timetables, agenda items, notes and wallpapers — remain with you or the original rights holder. You grant us the limited processing permissions necessary to provide local features to you (for example, storing and displaying them on your device).
legal.terms.s7.heading: 7. Disclaimers and Limitation of Liability
legal.terms.s7.body: This app is provided on an “as is” and “as available” basis. To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for: failures, interface changes or maintenance downtime of the university's or a third party's systems; network interruptions or device-compatibility problems; problems caused by your not updating the app in time; or the consequences of decisions you make — such as course selection, bookings or travel — in reliance on the displayed data.

For operations involving money or quotas — such as bookings, payments and the campus card — the university's or bank's pages and official records are ultimately authoritative. Balances, orders, seat statuses and similar information shown in this app are for reference only.

To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any indirect, incidental or punitive losses. If we are nonetheless held liable under law, our liability is capped at the fees you actually paid in relation to the dispute (if any); where use is free of charge, our liability is limited to what the law mandatorily requires.
legal.terms.s8.heading: 8. Service Changes, Suspension and Termination
legal.terms.s8.body: We may change, suspend or discontinue some or all features for reasons of product iteration, compliance requirements or operational needs, and we will give notice through in-app announcements, the website or other reasonable means.

You may stop using and uninstall the app at any time. After uninstalling, data in the device's local cache and secure storage may be cleared by the system's own mechanisms; for the handling of cloud account data, see the Privacy Policy.
legal.terms.s9.heading: 9. Agreement Updates and Governing Law
legal.terms.s9.body: We may update this agreement. Updated versions will be published on this site, and the “Last updated” date at the bottom of the page is authoritative. If a change affects your material rights, we will try to notify you by reasonable means. If you continue to use the app after an update, you are deemed to accept the updated content.

The formation, validity, interpretation and dispute resolution of this agreement are governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China (excluding its conflict-of-laws rules). Disputes should be resolved through friendly negotiation; if negotiation fails, they will be submitted to the competent people's court at the place of our principal operations (except where the law mandatorily provides otherwise).
legal.terms.s10.heading: 10. Contact Us
legal.terms.s10.body: If you have any questions about this agreement, you can contact us through the ClosedWHU community channels (such as the ClosedWHU GitHub organisation, or the community entry points published in the app or on the website).
legal.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
legal.privacy.description: Explains how Luotopia collects, uses, stores and protects your personal information, and the rights you have.
legal.privacy.s1.heading: 1. Introduction
legal.privacy.s1.body: ClosedWHU Team (hereinafter “we”, “us” or “our”) values user privacy. This policy explains how we process personal information when you use the Luotopia client and related services, and how you can exercise your rights.

The design principle of this app is that academic and campus-life data is handled mainly by “on-device processing and on-device caching”; only when you use features that need a network connection — such as accounts, AI, weather, wallpapers or the open interfaces — does the app send to the relevant servers the data necessary to make those features work.
Please read this policy together with the Terms of Service and the Cross-Border Data Transfer Notice. If you do not agree with this policy, please stop using the app.
legal.privacy.s2.heading: 2. Types of Information We Process
legal.privacy.s2.sub1.heading: 2.1 Campus Identity and Session Information (Usually Stored Only On-Device)
legal.privacy.s2.sub1.body: After you sign in through CAS, the app may store locally on your device: CAS session cookies (which may include session-ticket fields), business cookies for systems such as academic affairs, sign-in and verification timestamps, and student-status display information obtained from the university's interfaces (such as your student ID number, name, school, major, class and year of study, following whatever the university actually returns). This information is used to keep you signed in and to call features such as grades, timetables, free classrooms, venues, the library and messages. By default it is not uploaded to Luotopia's own business servers.
legal.privacy.s2.sub2.heading: 2.2 Academic and Campus Business Data (Mostly Cached On-Device)
legal.privacy.s2.sub2.body: This includes but is not limited to: timetables and timetable-import data, grades and GPA-related data, academic progress, free-classroom search results, library seat-booking records, sports-venue bookings and order information, campus messages, shuttle-bus route and location data, and university-calendar display data. This data comes from Wuhan University's systems, is obtained with the authorisation of your sign-in session, and is mainly cached on your device so that it can be shown offline or faster.
legal.privacy.s2.sub3.heading: 2.3 Luojia E-card / Payment-Related
legal.privacy.s2.sub3.body: The E-card and payment-code features may reach Smart Luojia, the mobile gateway and pages related to the China Construction Bank campus card through a WebView or an interface chain. This process may involve session cookies, redirect parameters and bank-side identifiers (such as `USERID` and `SKEY`, following the actual chain). Payment and the handling of funds are completed by the bank's or the university's systems; we do not store your bank-card password or payment passcode.
legal.privacy.s2.sub4.heading: 2.4 Luotopia Account Information (If You Register / Sign In)
legal.privacy.s2.sub4.body: This may include your username, password (submitted to the server over a secure connection), optional email address, tokens, and profile fields (such as display name, bio and avatar, following the fields actually made available). It is used for account authentication and for the optional community and open capabilities. The server keeps a session record for each sign-in, which usually contains the sign-in IP address, the client User-Agent (including the app version and platform), the device identifier and the runtime-environment security conclusion (see 2.9); this is used to show you the “Signed-in devices” list and to let you revoke the corresponding sessions.
legal.privacy.s2.sub5.heading: 2.5 Local Content You Create
legal.privacy.s2.sub5.body: Agenda items, to-dos, notes, course-editing data, wallpaper choices, and preferences such as theme and language. These are saved on your device by default; notes and wallpapers may read album images that you authorise.
legal.privacy.s2.sub6.heading: 2.6 AI Assistant-Related
legal.privacy.s2.sub6.body: Conversation content, session history, the API key you configure, and your provider and model settings. The API key is kept in the system's secure storage; conversation content can be stored encrypted on your device. For what is sent to the AI provider, see Section 4 and the Cross-Border Data Transfer Notice.
legal.privacy.s2.sub7.heading: 2.7 Location and Weather
legal.privacy.s2.sub7.body: When you grant location permission, the app may use your precise or approximate location to provide weather and shuttle-bus-stop experiences; if you do not grant location permission, it may use an approximate, IP-based location. Weather data may come from a source you choose or from a default one, such as Open-Meteo, Mi Weather or AccuWeather, and is cached on your device.
legal.privacy.s2.sub8.heading: 2.8 Device and Permission-Related Information
legal.privacy.s2.sub8.body: To provide features such as notification reminders, exact alarms, Bluetooth watch pairing and album reading, the system may request the corresponding permissions from you. We will not collect data unrelated to the features — such as your contacts or text messages — without saying so.
legal.privacy.s2.sub9.heading: 2.9 Device Identifiers, Signed-In Devices and Security Checks
legal.privacy.s2.sub9.body: So that you can tell your own devices apart and manage them in the “Signed-in devices” list, the client generates a random installation identifier (a UUID). This identifier contains no personal information in itself and is not linked to your campus identity; the authoritative copy of it is kept in the system's secure storage (such as the Android Keystore, the iOS Secure Enclave, or a desktop platform's key store). The client also reports the device name (on Android the manufacturer and model; on iOS the model's marketing name; on Windows and macOS the computer name; on Linux the distribution name), the platform, the system version and the app version. These fields are submitted with the sign-in request and synced to the current session after a successful sign-in and on a cold start; you can revoke any device's session at any time.

The client has built-in runtime-environment security checks: on Android and iOS it uses the third-party SDK freeRASP (Talsec / AHEAD), and on desktop platforms it uses a local probe. The check conclusion (normal, at risk, app data cloned, or checks not supported on this platform) and the risk-type labels (such as root or jailbreak, injection frameworks, an attached debugger, an emulator, a tampered app signature, or running with administrator or root privileges) are reported to our server and shown in your own “Signed-in devices” list. To carry out its detection of malicious and hidden apps, this SDK may read information about some of the apps installed on the device.

Please note: these conclusions are reference information reported by the device itself and are used only to help you spot abnormal sign-ins and abnormal devices. We will not take action such as banning you on the basis of this information alone. On platforms that do not support the checks, the list will show “No data” or “Not supported” rather than recording them as “Secure”.

When the security SDK determines that the app data has been copied to another device, the client clears the credentials in this device's secure storage and regenerates the installation identifier, which signs you out. This measure runs locally and is meant to protect the security of your account.
The raw details collected by the desktop-platform probe (such as the system username and user groups) are shown only on a local developer page on the device and are not reported to our server.
legal.privacy.s2.sub10.heading: 2.10 Logs and Debugging Information
legal.privacy.s2.sub10.body: Development and debugging builds may output logs such as network status and error information (for example via `debugPrint`). The app also maintains a rolling diagnostic log file on the device, which usually contains timestamps, feature modules, network status and error summaries; this log is kept only on your device and leaves it only when you actively export or share it.

We have integrated three optional channels provided by Google Firebase: Analytics, Crashlytics and Performance. The corresponding toggles in Settings are off by default; the onboarding page shown on first launch presents a consent option for diagnostics and analytics, which is ticked by default. You can untick it before finishing onboarding, and you can turn it on or off at any time afterwards under “Settings → Privacy”. Collection begins only once you turn it on, and what may be collected includes crash and exception records (including the call stack and the reason for failure), together with the usage-analytics and performance data you choose to enable. On Android devices without Google Play services, Firebase is not initialised at all. After you turn it off, we stop any new collection; the processing of data already submitted is governed by Google's relevant rules.
If the server enables audit logs, rate limiting or human verification (such as Altcha), these are used only for security and operations, and not to sell user profiles.
legal.privacy.s3.heading: 3. Where and How Information Is Stored
legal.privacy.s3.body: On-device secure storage (wrapping system capabilities such as the Android Keystore / iOS Keychain): the Luotopia sign-in token and user profile, the AI API key, campus-authentication snapshots (cookies and the like), and the local encryption master key.
On-device encrypted storage: sensitive local data such as AI conversations can be encrypted at the application layer before being written to preference storage.
Ordinary on-device preferences and files: settings, timetables, agenda items, weather and shuttle-bus caches, grade-import caches, wallpaper files and metadata, and the onboarding-completion state.
WebView cookies: used to keep you signed in to CAS and to the various campus business sites.

Cloud: only when you use a Luotopia account, or cloud community / review features that may be enabled in the future, is the related data stored on our servers or those of a party we entrust (the client connects by default to `api-whu-sb.tsinbei.cn`; `api.whu.sb` has also been used in the past). By default, academic-affairs data is not uploaded for the purpose of “syncing to our cloud”. The session records kept on the server usually contain the sign-in IP address, the client User-Agent, the device identifier and device name, platform and version information, the runtime-environment security conclusion, and the device note you fill in yourself.
legal.privacy.s4.heading: 4. How We Use Information
legal.privacy.s4.body: To provide and maintain the features you choose to use (sign-in, lookup, booking entry points, display, reminders, AI conversations and so on);
To cache data on your device in order to reduce repeated requests and improve performance and the experience on weak networks;
To safeguard the security of accounts and sessions and to guard against abuse and attacks;
To improve the product experience (based on overall feature needs, not on selling personal data);
To fulfil the obligations set out in laws and regulations.
We do not sell your personal information.
legal.privacy.s5.heading: 5. Entrusted Processing, Sharing and Third Parties
legal.privacy.s5.body: Operators of the campus systems: when you use CAS sign-in and the various campus features, Wuhan University and the relevant systems (for example `cas.whu.edu.cn`, `jwgl.whu.edu.cn`, `zyfzzd.whu.edu.cn`, `zhlj.whu.edu.cn`, `zsgx.whu.edu.cn`, `gym.whu.edu.cn`, `seat.lib.whu.edu.cn`, `bus.whu.edu.cn`, `msgp.whu.edu.cn` and `pay.whu.edu.cn`, among others) process your identity and business data according to their own rules. We cannot control the privacy practices of the university's systems, so we suggest that you also read the university's own notices.

Banks and payment-related parties: scenarios such as the E-card payment code may involve services related to the China Construction Bank campus card (such as `app.xiaoyuan.ccb.com`), to which the bank's own rules apply.

Weather and geo services: Open-Meteo, Mi Weather, AccuWeather, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and IP-geolocation services (such as `api.ip.sb` and `ip-api.com`) receive location or query parameters only when a feature needs them.
Wallpaper services: the Bing daily wallpaper may request Bing's relevant interfaces and cache the image on your device.
AI providers: the large-model API you choose receives the conversation and the agenda-summary context.

Security-check SDK: freeRASP (Talsec / AHEAD), used for runtime-environment integrity and device-binding checks. This SDK reports security events to its provider's back end; separately, we provide the random installation identifier generated by the client (see 2.9) to that provider as an external id, so that security events can be matched to the same device on our side. What is reported does not include your campus credentials, account passwords or chat content; security-alert emails are received at `security@whu.sb`. This provider's servers may be located overseas.

Push services: Google Firebase Cloud Messaging (`fcm.googleapis.com`), and Huawei Push Kit on devices without Google Play services. Our server stores the push token and the installation identifier in order to deliver notifications to you. Push is on by default and you can turn it off in Settings; once you turn it off, the client deletes the push token and stops registering.

IP-location lookup: when you open the “Signed-in devices” list, the client queries `ip9.com.cn` directly for the location and carrier of the IP addresses in the list, in order to show the “Region / carrier”. This request is sent by your device and does not pass through our server; it contains nothing beyond the IP address and the usual request headers. This service is located within mainland China.

Infrastructure and content distribution: the website, static resources and the friend-links configuration may be distributed through platforms such as Cloudflare; the server may use human verification such as Altcha.
Open-source and collaboration links: visits to GitHub, Weblate and similar sites are triggered by you, and the corresponding platform's policies apply.
Except where necessary to make a feature work, where we have your consent, or where the law requires it, we do not share personal information that can identify you with unrelated third parties.
legal.privacy.s6.heading: 6. Permissions
legal.privacy.s6.body: Network: to access the campus systems, weather, AI, website configuration and so on;
Location: for weather, shuttle-bus and related experiences (you can refuse; some features will be reduced);
Notifications and exact alarms: for class and agenda reminders;
Album / media reading: for wallpaper and note images;
Biometrics: for the optional grades privacy lock;
You can manage permissions in the system settings; refusing a non-essential permission usually does not affect other, unrelated features.
legal.privacy.s7.heading: 7. Information Security and Retention Periods
legal.privacy.s7.body: We take reasonable technical measures to protect sensitive local data (for example through the system's secure storage and application-layer encryption) and the security of data in transit (for example HTTPS; a few of the university's or compatibility-related links may still use legacy compatibility configurations).

How long the local cache is retained depends on whether you sign out, clear the cache or uninstall the app. Cloud account data is retained for as long as the business needs require, until you close your account or it must be deleted by law.

The validity period of cloud tokens and sessions follows the server configuration and is usually as follows: an access token is valid for 15 minutes; a refresh token and a session are each valid for 720 hours (30 days), and each use during that period slides the expiry forward. If there is no activity for more than 30 days, the corresponding session and refresh token both expire and you need to sign in again.
Please note: no security measure can guarantee absolute security, so please strengthen the protection of your device.
legal.privacy.s8.heading: 8. Your Rights
legal.privacy.s8.body: Access and copy: you can view the cached content in the app, such as your timetable, grades and agenda;
Correct and delete: you can edit your local agenda and timetable, sign out of the campus account to stop using the corresponding cookies, or uninstall the app to clear the data on your device;
Withdraw consent: you can turn off permissions such as location, notifications and album access, or stop using optional features such as the AI and weather;

Session management: on the “Signed-in devices” page you can see the sessions of each device under your current account, revoke a single device's session, or revoke all sessions at once; if you change your password or your email address, all sessions under that account are revoked automatically and you need to sign in again on each device;

Account matters: if you use a Luotopia account, you can contact us through the published channels to handle account-closure or correction requests (subject to identity verification and to the extent permitted by law).
Display controls such as the grades privacy lock and spoiler protection are local experience features; they do not change the processing rules of the party the data comes from.
legal.privacy.s9.heading: 9. Minors
legal.privacy.s9.body: This app is aimed mainly at students and staff of higher-education institutions. If you are a minor, please read this policy and use the app under the guidance of a guardian.
legal.privacy.s10.heading: 10. Policy Updates
legal.privacy.s10.body: We may update this policy from time to time, and the “Last updated” date on this page is authoritative. For material changes, we will try to notify you by reasonable means such as the website or in-app prompts.
legal.privacy.s11.heading: 11. Contact Us
legal.privacy.s11.body: If you have questions, complaints or requests about this policy or about the processing of your personal information, please contact us through the ClosedWHU community channels (such as the ClosedWHU GitHub organisation or the entry point published on the website).
legal.cross-border.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer Notice
legal.cross-border.description: Explains the overseas recipients, transfer scenarios and choices that may be involved when you use Luotopia.
legal.cross-border.s1.heading: 1. Purpose of This Notice
legal.cross-border.s1.body: This notice tells you which features may, in the course of providing Luotopia's services, cause your data to be transferred to servers outside the People's Republic of China or processed through overseas nodes, so that you can decide whether to use those features on a fully informed basis.

Campus unified authentication and most business requests — for academic affairs, venues, the library, the shuttle bus and the like — are sent by default to Wuhan University and to the domains of partner systems within mainland China, and are not the “active cross-border” scenarios that this notice mainly addresses; but accessing the website, weather, wallpapers, some AI providers, code hosting and CDNs may involve cross-border processing.
legal.cross-border.s2.heading: 2. Scenarios and Recipients That May Involve Cross-Border Transfers
legal.cross-border.s2.sub1.heading: 2.1 Weather and Geocoding (Optional / Depends on Provider)
legal.cross-border.s2.sub1.body: Open-Meteo (such as `api.open-meteo.com`, `air-quality-api.open-meteo.com` and `geocoding-api.open-meteo.com`): may receive latitude-and-longitude or place-name queries, used for forecasts and air quality. Its service facilities are usually located overseas.
AccuWeather (`api.accuweather.com`): if you choose this source or the system uses it, query parameters and location-related information may be sent overseas.
OpenStreetMap Nominatim (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org`): reverse-geocoding requests may be sent overseas.

Coarse IP-based location (such as `api.ip.sb` and `ip-api.com`): when GPS is not authorised, or a fallback location is needed, the app may query the relevant service for an approximate, IP-based location; these services may be located overseas or reached through overseas routes.

Domestic sources such as Mi Weather (`weatherapi.market.xiaomi.com`): these generally do not constitute the cross-border transfer described in this section, but the actual DNS resolution and network path are authoritative.
legal.cross-border.s2.sub2.heading: 2.2 Wallpapers and Content Distribution
legal.cross-border.s2.sub2.body: Bing daily wallpaper (`www.bing.com` and related interfaces): when requesting wallpaper metadata or images, the app may reach Microsoft's relevant overseas infrastructure and cache the image file on your device.
legal.cross-border.s2.sub3.heading: 2.3 AI Large Models (Configured by the User)
legal.cross-border.s2.sub3.body: When you set the AI provider to OpenAI (`api.openai.com`), Anthropic (`api.anthropic.com`), Google Gemini (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`), xAI (`api.x.ai`), Perplexity (`api.perplexity.ai`) or another overseas or custom overseas address, your conversation content, message history and local agenda-summary fields are transferred to the corresponding overseas server.

If you use a default or optional provider that is based within mainland China or whose main site is within mainland China — such as SiliconFlow, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Zhipu AI, Tongyi or Hunyuan — this generally does not constitute a cross-border transfer in the sense of this section; the provider's actual deployment and privacy policy are ultimately authoritative. The model gateway built into the app, `ai.tsinbei.cn`, is our own first-party service (within mainland China).
legal.cross-border.s2.sub4.heading: 2.4 Official Website, Static Resources and Security Verification
legal.cross-border.s2.sub4.body: Luotopia's website and some static resources (such as the `whu.sb` site, the friend-links JSON, the legal text and app screenshots) may be hosted on Cloudflare Pages or distributed through the Cloudflare network, and the access logs and requests may pass through overseas nodes.

The client itself also actively requests `www.whu.sb` to obtain the legal text and catalogue, the font mirror, the hot-update script manifest, the friend-links configuration and app-update information; these requests are likewise distributed through the Cloudflare network and may generate standard access logs (IP, User-Agent and request path). Among these, our Pages Function reverse proxy forwards font requests to `fonts.gstatic.com`.
The server uses Altcha human verification, whose proof-of-work is completed on the client and verified by the server.
legal.cross-border.s2.sub5.heading: 2.5 Developer and Community Resources (Accessed by the User)
legal.cross-border.s2.sub5.body: GitHub (`github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com` and the like): when you view the source code, releases, hot-update scripts or documentation, the requests go overseas.

Google Noto Sans font: unlike the resources above that you actively access, the font is a default interface resource that is usually loaded on demand in the background. When the client needs this font, it first tries to obtain it from our own first-party source `www.whu.sb/fonts/gstatic/` (this source reverse-proxies `fonts.gstatic.com` through Cloudflare Pages, the file names are their SHA-256 digests, and the client verifies the digest and the file length); only when this mirror is unavailable does it connect directly to `fonts.gstatic.com`, in which case a cross-border request may occur.

iOS and macOS use the system fonts by default and usually do not download any fonts at all; devices whose system already includes the chosen font likewise do not download it. The MiSans font is obtained on demand from `www.whu.sb/fonts/misans/`. The fonts used by the website itself are all self-hosted and do not make requests to Google.
legal.cross-border.s2.sub6.heading: 2.6 Friend Links and Third-Party Apps
legal.cross-border.s2.sub6.body: After you click a friend link and go to a third-party website or app (such as a club site, a partner app or an AI sign-up page), that third party's privacy and cross-border rules apply, so please read them carefully.
legal.cross-border.s2.sub7.heading: 2.7 Security Checks and Push Services
legal.cross-border.s2.sub7.body: Security checks: freeRASP (Talsec / AHEAD) reports security events to that provider's back end, and we separately provide the random installation identifier generated by the client (a UUID) to that provider as an external id, so that security events can be matched to the same device; its servers may be located overseas.

Push services: the push token for Google Firebase Cloud Messaging (`fcm.googleapis.com`) is forwarded to Google via our server, and the related processing may take place overseas; on devices without Google Play services, Huawei Push Kit (within mainland China) may be used instead.

Optional telemetry: only after you turn it on in the onboarding page or in Settings are the crash and exception records, usage analytics and performance data from Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics and Performance sent to Google, whose servers are usually located overseas; these three channels are off by default.
None of the transfers described above include your campus account credentials, passwords, detailed grades or chat content. For the related processing, see the Privacy Policy.
legal.cross-border.s3.heading: 3. Scope of Transferred Information (Minimised)
legal.cross-border.s3.body: Weather / geo: location coordinates or a city name, the IP (for coarse location), and request metadata such as the device time zone and language;
Wallpapers: requests for the wallpaper list or image URLs, generally without any campus-account cookies;
AI: chat text, agenda-summary fields, the model name and the API key (the key is provided by you and stored on your device, and is submitted with the request to the provider you choose);
Website / CDN: standard web access logs (IP, User-Agent, the path accessed and the like);
Security checks: risk-type labels, the check conclusion and the random installation identifier;
Push: the push token, the installation identifier, the platform and version, and the language and time zone;
By default, CAS passwords, academic-affairs cookies and detailed grades are not uploaded in bulk to overseas weather or wallpaper services.
legal.cross-border.s4.heading: 4. Purpose and Legal Basis
legal.cross-border.s4.body: Cross-border transfers happen only to make the features you actively use work (obtaining forecasts, wallpapers, AI replies, accessing documentation or the website and so on), or to safeguard the security and availability of the site.

You give your consent by turning on the relevant permissions, by choosing an overseas data source or AI provider, or by actively following an overseas link; you can also refuse or stop this through “Your choices” below.
legal.cross-border.s5.heading: 5. Security and Safeguards
legal.cross-border.s5.body: We use encrypted transport such as HTTPS wherever possible;
Sensitive credentials are kept first in the system's secure storage, and AI conversations can be stored encrypted on your device;
The choice of overseas provider is left to you (especially for the AI);
Core campus business connects by default directly to the university's systems within mainland China, reducing unnecessary cross-border transfers.
We require or expect third parties to protect data within the scope of what their own policies promise, but a third party's independent processing is its own responsibility.
legal.cross-border.s6.heading: 6. Your Choices
legal.cross-border.s6.body: Refuse location permission and avoid using features that rely on overseas weather sources; in Settings, prefer a weather data source within mainland China (where one is available);
Do not use the Bing wallpaper source; use a local image instead, or turn wallpapers off;
For the AI, use only providers within mainland China, or turn off the AI assistant; do not provide sensitive personal information in the conversation;
Do not follow overseas links such as GitHub;
If you do not agree to the cross-border processing described in this notice, please stop using the relevant features or uninstall the app.
legal.cross-border.s7.heading: 7. Updates to This Notice
legal.cross-border.s7.body: The list of overseas recipients may change as versions iterate or as the default providers or infrastructure are adjusted. The updated notice is authoritative as of the “Last updated” date on this page and is published on this site. We suggest that you review it from time to time.
For the machine-readable catalogue, see `/data/legal.json` (it contains each document's slug, title and `lastUpdated`, so that the client can check versions).
legal.cross-border.s8.heading: 8. Contact Us
legal.cross-border.s8.body: If you have questions about cross-border processing, please contact us through the ClosedWHU community channels.
